mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an easing monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales growth signal broad consumer demand weakness that triggers corporate revenue revisions downward, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production signals manufacturing output contraction that reduces corporate profit margins and triggers economic slowdown expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real retail sales growth over the past month indicates strong consumer spending that supports corporate revenue expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS increases, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% signals persistent inflation that prompts Federal Reserve tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations for negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in non-farm payrolls and unemployment rate indicate labor market contraction that reduces consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both PAYEMS and UNRATE decline, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles, federal funds rate increases above 0.5% signal restrictive policy that raises borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during tightening cycles when FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.
